# **ARDUINO-BASED DISTANCE MEASUREMENT USING ULTRASONIC SENSOR**

# **1\. Aim**

To measure the distance of an object using an **Arduino and ultrasonic sensor**.

# **2\. Components Required**

1. Arduino Board  
2. Ultrasonic Sensor (HC-SR04)  
3. Connecting Wires  
4. Breadboard

# **3\. Principle**

The ultrasonic sensor measures distance by sending ultrasonic waves and detecting the time taken for the reflected waves to return.

# **4\. Working**

The Arduino sends a trigger signal to the ultrasonic sensor. The sensor sends ultrasonic waves towards the object and receives the reflected waves. The Arduino calculates the distance based on the time taken for the echo to return and displays the measured distance in centimetres on the Serial Monitor.![][image1]

# **5\. Arduino Code**

const int trigPin \= 9;  
const int echoPin \= 10;

long duration;  
float distance;

void setup() {  
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);  
  Serial.begin(9600);  
}

void loop() {  
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);  
  delayMicroseconds(2);

  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);  
  delayMicroseconds(10);  
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  duration \= pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);

  distance \= duration \* 0.034 / 2;

  Serial.print("Distance: ");  
  Serial.print(distance);  
  Serial.println(" cm");

  delay(500);  
}![][image2]

# **6\. Applications**

* Distance measurement  
* Object detection  
* Obstacle detection  
* Robotics  
* Smart parking systems

# **7\. Result**

The distance of an object was successfully measured using the **Arduino and HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor** and displayed on the Serial Monitor.![][image3]

# **8\. Conclusion**

The project successfully demonstrated **real-time distance measurement using an Arduino and ultrasonic sensor**, providing practical experience in sensor int
